chunks: Certainly, Allāh tests His servants when they commit evil deeds
by decreasing fruits, holding back blessings, and closing the treasures of goodness
so that the repentant may repent, the one turning away may turn away, the mindful may be mindful, and the heedful may take heed.
And Allāh, the Glorified, has made seeking forgiveness a means for the pouring down of livelihood and mercy upon the creation
so He said: 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.'
He will send [down from] the sky rain in pouring showers.
And give you wealth and children
And make for you gardens and make for you rivers.
ai.seo_question: How does seeking forgiveness lead to increased provision and mercy according to Shia teachings?
ai.summary: In this sermon from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the theological concept of *adab al-du'a* (etiquette of supplication), framing material scarcity not as punishment but as a merciful pedagogical tool to awaken spiritual mindfulness. He establishes a causal link between *istighfar* (seeking forgiveness) and the removal of veils from divine bounty, citing Surah Nuh to illustrate how repentance unlocks the gates of rain, wealth, and progeny. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between spiritual purification and worldly prosperity as signs of divine favor.
